title: Unions and shared storage
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or resource flow.
Recognize relevant safety and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A union is a type whose members share the same storage region. Its size is sufficient for its largest member, with alignment requirements. At a given time, a program generally interprets the stored representation through the member most recently written, subject to C's specific rules.
understand.whyItMatters: Unions can represent variant data compactly, but reading an inactive member requires careful attention to the language rules and representation assumptions.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
A union is a type whose members share the same storage region. Its size is sufficient for its largest member, with alignment requirements. At a given time, a program generally interprets the stored representation through the member most recently written, subject to C's specific rules.

Check all allocation, I/O and conversion results. Respect object bounds and lifetime, initialize data before reading it, and define who owns and releases each resource.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The union has storage shared by whole and decimal. The example writes and reads whole; it does not assume that the same bytes form a portable float value.

practise.guidedTask: Explain why the two members do not occupy separate storage within one union object.
practise.independentTask: Create a tagged union with an enum indicating which member is active. Write code that reads only the selected member.
hints: A union's size may exceed the size of its largest member because of alignment and padding.
Use a separate tag when the program needs to track which variant is active.
Do not assume arbitrary type-punning through a union is portable across every implementation.
